name: ANSI/IEEE coaxial cable symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented coaxial cable drawn as a centre conductor with a surrounding outer conductor that terminates at each end.
description: IEEE-oriented drawings represent coaxial cable with a centre line enclosed by an outer conductor outline, often with the outer conductor brought out to a ground or connector shell at the ends. The convention is used on communications, metering time-sync and RF schematics in US-practice drawing sets.

This illustration explains the idea and is not a certified IEEE graphic. The cable impedance and connector types must still be given in text. Where the outer conductor is grounded at both ends between buildings, check for ground loop and surge transfer issues.
readingNotes: Read connector and impedance notes at each end.
Check outer conductor grounding at building entries.
distinction: The ANSI coaxial form has a current-carrying outer conductor; the ANSI shielded conductor form has a screen only.
